items.title: Verstappen wins a rain-hit Sepang race for Red Bull's first victory of 2026
items.summary: Verstappen converted pole into the win from Antonelli (+2.307s) and Hamilton (+4.919s), with Leclerc fourth and Hadjar fifth. A heavy downpour delayed the start; Hamilton and Leclerc started on slicks, fell back, then recovered to the podium and P4. Piastri, Lawson, Alonso, Norris and Lindblad completed the points.
items.why_it_matters: It is Red Bull's breakthrough win of the season and a decisive tyre-call story: the intermediate-to-slick switch window punished those who started on slicks, yet Ferrari's recoveries still produced a podium.

items.title: FIA software bug caused power loss on the formation lap; update issued during the delay
items.summary: The FIA said an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy-management settings and Sepang's sector layout caused an unintended loss of power on a number of cars. It released updated software removing the energy-limit constraint in the affected sectors during the rain delay and will review the issue with teams and PU manufacturers. Nikolas Tombazis said the code had little wet-running testing.
items.why_it_matters: A regulation-linked software fault, not driver error, disrupted the start procedure. The promised full review could bring changes to energy-management settings for future wet races.

items.title: Russell's late power-unit failure hands Antonelli the title momentum
items.summary: Russell was battling Antonelli for second when his Mercedes stopped on the start/finish straight behind the final Safety Car, classified 20th. Formula1.com says Antonelli was already set to extend his championship lead over Russell by three points before the retirement. Toto Wolff called it a PU failure not caused by the Safety Car, 'one of my worst experiences', and stressed the DNFs as a risk for the remaining seven races.
items.why_it_matters: It is Russell's third retirement of the year and Mercedes' fourth, hurting both his title chances and the constructors' fight. Mercedes has yet to assess the cause. Use the timestamped standings table for current totals.

items.title: Bortoleto penalised after Sainz contact; Norris loses control behind the Safety Car
items.summary: Bortoleto and Sainz collided on a mid-race restart and Bortoleto received a 10-second penalty. Norris ran through the gravel behind the final Safety Car and finished ninth. Albon's stoppage with a gearbox failure brought out the late Safety Car; Bottas's lap-nine spin caused the earlier one.
items.why_it_matters: The restart order and Safety Car periods reshaped the points positions, costing Williams a strong early run and McLaren a chance at fifth and sixth.
